Pillar 4 · Smart-Contracts
State machine + extensible conditions + early order creation

A Smart-Contract is the source of truth.
The order is a downstream effect.

When the customer clicks “Place Order”, Payment Base does not create an order — it creates a PaymentContract. The contract carries an immutable BasketSnapshot and a list of conditions that must be fulfilled before commitment. The order is created early (in NOT_FINISHED state) so its order number is available before redirecting to the PSP.

Why early order creation
  • Order number available before the PSP session is created
  • PSP dashboard (Stripe / PayPal) shows the order number in metadata — reconciliation works on day 1
  • Order exists before payment completion — no race with webhooks
  • Order finalisation (COMMITTED) only when all conditions are met
Conditions are extensible
$contract->addCondition(
    new ContractCondition(
        type: 'subscription_verified',
        data: ['plan_id' => 'pro_monthly']
    )
);

// Later, in your event handler:
$contract->fulfilCondition(
    'subscription_verified',
    ['verified_at' => '2026-05-08T10:23:00Z']
);

// When ALL conditions are fulfilled:
//   ContractReadyToCommitEvent dispatched
//   StripeOrderCreationHandler / your handler finalises
The hook points are the state transitions. Each Contract…Event is a place your extension can intercept. Your code never mutates a contract directly — you dispatch an event, a handler mutates. Grep guards in one-page-checkout/bin/pre-commit-check.sh enforce this.
